fields.meta_description: Build a copyright release form that names the work and each right granted, then captures an e-signature from the owner. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Copyright Release Form That Names Every Right Granted
fields.hero_description: Build a copyright release form that lists each right granted, captures the owner's e-signature, and saves every signed release.
fields.features_heading: What a Copyright Release Has to Name
fields.features_subheading: A copyright release form names the work and the rights it grants. These six pieces turn each release into a record you can search.
fields.feature_1:
License or transfer, chosen first

The owner picks whether they are granting permission to use the work or handing over the copyright itself. The form then shows only the wording for that choice and saves the pick.
fields.feature_2:
The exact work, down to the file

Each release records the work's title and its file name or catalog number, with an upload of the image itself. Nobody has to guess which of 300 photos a release covers.
fields.feature_3:
One line per right granted

Printing, editing, posting online, and public display each get their own checkbox, with a term in years and a territory beside them. The owner ticks only the rights they grant.
fields.feature_4:
Every release in one searchable table

Each signed release becomes a row in a database you own, with the work, the rights ticked, the signer, and the date. Search by file name when a print shop asks to see one.
fields.feature_5:
An e-signature from the rights owner

The owner adds an e-signature from a phone or laptop, and the app records the signer's name and the date beside it. Both parties get an email copy of the signed release.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the release app's full code to your GitHub repository on paid plans. A developer can then host it on your own servers or connect it to the gallery system you already run.

fields.tab_content_1:
A print release for all 40 gallery files

Halden Bay Portraits delivers a 40-image gallery, and client Sefa Adjei asks for a print release from the gallery page. The photographer signs one that names all 40 files and allows personal prints only, while the copyright stays with the studio. Sefa gets the signed release by email to show the print shop.
fields.tab_content_2:
With a co-owner named, an entry waits for both

Every entry to the Juniper Hall Arts Guild spring show includes a short release. Each artist lets the guild reproduce the work in its printed catalog and on its website, and confirms they own it. This year 64 artists entered. Two entries named a co-owner, and the guild held both until the co-owner signed too.
fields.tab_content_3:
On full payment of $2,400, the logo transfers

Ashcombe Studio's contract with Saffron Pier Coffee moves the copyright in the final logo to the client on full payment. When the studio marks the $2,400 final invoice paid, the studio owner gets the transfer to sign, and Saffron Pier receives the signed copy. The 3 rejected concepts stay with the studio.
fields.tab_content_4:
For 2 of 11 figures, Maren gets a reminder

Chapter 3 of Maren Holt's dissertation reuses 11 figures from published papers. One form sends each publisher a permission request and logs every reply against its figure. So far 9 of the 11 requests have been granted. With 14 days to the library deadline, Maren gets an email naming the 2 that have not answered.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Copyright Release Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a copyright release form that names the work, each right, and the signer, then build it with Emergent.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Choose a license or a transfer
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Confirm who has the right to sign
fields.howto_step_1_des: Decide whether the release licenses the work or transfers ownership of the copyright, since the wording differs for each. Keep a separate template for each choice, and have your attorney review the release wording before the first one goes out.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Name the work so precisely that nobody can mistake it: title, creation date, file name or catalog number, and an image of it. For a gallery or a series, list every file the release covers instead of writing every photo from the session.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Write each use you need as its own line, such as prints for sale, edits, or use on a website. Under 17 U.S.C. 201(d)(2), any of the exclusive rights, including any subdivision of them, may be transferred and owned separately. Give each line a term and a territory.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Ask the signer to confirm they own the rights or are signing for the owner, and to name anyone who made the work with them. Store each answer as its own field, so a co-owner who has not signed shows up before you use the work.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Describe the parties and the rights checklist in plain English, and say who signs. Emergent builds the form, the database behind it, and a page listing every release. Change any part later by describing the change in a new prompt.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add an e-signature for the owner, and one for you if the release needs both sides. Ask for an email copy to each party once the last signature is in, and a reminder to anyone who has not signed after 3 days.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Sign a test release before you send the link out. Check that the license or transfer choice shows the right wording, that each ticked right landed in its own field, and that the email copy arrived with your name and the date.

faq_plan.q: What is a copyright release form?
faq_plan.a: A copyright release form is a signed document in which the owner of a photo, artwork, or piece of writing lets someone else use it in named ways, or hands over the copyright itself. It identifies the work, lists the rights granted, and records who signed and on what date.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a copyright release form?
faq_plan.a: Write down the work, the rights you need, and who signs, then describe them to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the release with an e-signature step and stores each signed copy in your own database. Ask for changes in plain English later, such as a new right or a second signer.

faq_plan.q: Can one copyright release form template cover both photos and artwork?
faq_plan.a: Yes, if the work section changes with the type. Keep the parties and the signature the same, then ask for a file name and shoot date on a photo and the medium and dimensions on a painting. Emergent builds that switch from a plain-English prompt, along with the logic behind it.

faq_plan.q: Where can I make a free copyright release form online?
faq_plan.a: You can build one on Emergent's free tier, which covers building and publishing the form. A copyright release form PDF from a template site also works for a single signature, but each new release means another file to fill in and store. When the photo shows a recognizable person, pair the release with a model release form signed by that person.

faq_plan.q: Do I need a copyright release form to print my professional photos?
faq_plan.hint: Do i need a copyright release form from mom354?
faq_plan.a: Ask for one when the photographer kept the copyright and your agreement does not already cover prints. Under 17 U.S.C. 106, and subject to sections 107 through 122, the copyright owner has the exclusive right to reproduce the work in copies. Get the print release in writing, naming your files, so you can show it to the print shop.

faq_plan.q: How do I ask a photographer to sign a copyright release form?
faq_plan.hint: Do i need a copyright release form from mom365?
faq_plan.a: Ask in writing and be specific: the gallery or file names, the uses you want, such as prints or a book cover, and how long you need them. Offer to send a release that lists only those uses. The photographer can then agree to each line instead of a blanket grant.

faq_plan.q: Can one form collect a copyright release and a photo release?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as two sections with their own signatures. The photographer signs the copyright section, which grants uses of the image, and the person pictured signs the photo release form section, which gives permission to publish their likeness. Keeping them apart lets you check each signature on its own.

faq_plan.q: What is the difference between a license and a transfer on a copyright release form?
faq_plan.a: An exclusive license counts as a transfer of ownership, and a nonexclusive license does not. 17 U.S.C. 101 defines a transfer of copyright ownership as an assignment, exclusive license, or other conveyance of a copyright or any of its exclusive rights, but not a nonexclusive license. Have your attorney review which one your release grants.

faq_plan.q: Does a copyright release form have to be signed to transfer ownership?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Apart from transfers by operation of law, 17 U.S.C. 204(a) says such a transfer is not valid unless it is in writing and signed by the owner of the rights conveyed or the owner's duly authorized agent. Ask your attorney how that applies to the release you plan to use.

faq_plan.q: Can an art show entry form include a copyright release?
faq_plan.a: Yes, as its own section with a checkbox for each use, such as the catalog and the website. Under 17 U.S.C. 201(a), the authors of a joint work are coowners of copyright in it. Ask each artist to name any co-author. If the show has a hands-on workshop, add a liability waiver form as a separate section. Forms built with Emergent carry no response caps on entries.

plan.angle: The top 10 is single documents: eForms and eSign photo copyright releases, a college art release PDF, Adobe's guide to photographer release types, Lightfolio's and Jotform's photography templates, a sample photograph release, Rocket Lawyer's photo release and the Copyright Office's forms index. Each fixes one set of clauses for one situation and none separates a license from a transfer of ownership, which US copyright law treats differently. This page quotes the statute on that difference and on who must sign, lays out what a release names (the work, each right, the signer), and shows the release as a form that saves every work, right and signature as a row, across four kinds of creative work.
